problems.comment:
Large quantities of fresh snow and the wind-drifted snow of the last two days are in some cases prone to triggering. Single winter sport participants can release avalanches. In particular on north and east facing slopes these can in isolated cases reach large size. 
 Backcountry touring calls for experience in the assessment of avalanche danger.
On grassy slopes numerous small and, in isolated cases, medium-sized gliding avalanches are to be expected. Caution is to be exercised in areas with glide cracks.

bulletin.snowpack: Weak layers prone to triggering are found especially in the layers of new and wind-drifted snow from the last few days. These will stabilize rapidly. Distinct, faceted weak layers are scarcely present.
bulletin.tendency:
Dry avalanches
The danger of dry avalanches will decrease. However, persons can release avalanches as before. Careful route selection is required.
Wet-snow avalanches
Gliding avalanches are possible at any time. Areas with glide cracks are to be avoided as far as possible.

problems.comment:
Large quantities of fresh snow and the wind-drifted snow of the last two days are in some cases prone to triggering. Single winter sport participants can release avalanches, including large ones. 
 Backcountry touring calls for experience in the assessment of avalanche danger.
On steep grassy slopes numerous gliding avalanches are to be expected, even large ones. Areas with glide cracks are to be avoided as far as possible.

bulletin.snowpack:
Snow depths are well above average. Over a wide area there is two to three times as much snow as is usual for the time of year. Weak layers prone to triggering are still found mainly in the sometimes thick layers of new and wind-drifted snow from recent days. These will stabilize rapidly. 
Above approximately 2600 m, on north- and east-facing slopes, there is still coarse-grained old snow in places at the snow base. This near-ground old snow is now overlain so thickly that fractures in near-ground layers of the snowpack are not very likely.
bulletin.tendency:
Dry avalanches
The danger of dry avalanches will gradually decrease. Single winter sport participants can release avalanches as before. Backcountry touring calls for experience in the assessment of avalanche danger.
Wet-snow avalanches
Gliding avalanches are possible at any time. Areas with glide cracks are to be avoided as far as possible.
